prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-looking view of a flat brick walkway where the camera wearer's own torso (0.2–0.5 m), swinging arms (0.4–0.7 m), and striding legs (0.7–1.3 m) are brightest at the bottom center, while surrounding pedestrians appear as mid-grey silhouettes against a dark ground plane roughly 1.5–2.5 m below and ahead. Across the five frames, it tracks a pedestrian in a plaid shirt and maroon pants moving from the upper-left in frame 2 (about 1.8 m away) to directly ahead in frame 3 (about 1.4 m) and left again in frame 4 (about 1.3 m), while another pedestrian in a red top and black pants enters on the right in frame 2 within roughly 0.8–1.2 m (near arm's reach of the wearer's right hand) and others in black pants remain 1.8–2.5 m ahead on the upper right in frames 3–5, spaced 1.5–2.5 m apart from the left-side pedestrian. All surrounding people are truncated by the top and side edges of the frame—leaving their heads and gaze directions completely out of view—though their leg orientations show them facing and walking broadly forward or diagonally across the wearer's path as the wearer walks forward and turns slightly left. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the continuous brightness gradient makes the vertical relief of the wearer's chest and the relative proximity of the encroaching pedestrian on the right in frame 2 immediately apparent against the visually busy brick pattern. However, the depth map is unreliable on the flat ground plane, which darkens abruptly toward the top corners as if receding into a void rather than sloping evenly, and it completely misses the distant pedestrians' feet in frame 1 as well as the shallow curb and drain grate in the upper left of frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete `person` masks on a black background, separating the camera wearer's own body at the bottom center (0.2–1.3 m from the camera) from the cropped lower bodies of surrounding pedestrians walking 0.8–2.5 m ahead on the left and right. Across the sequence, it captures a far-left foot in frame 1 (about 2 m away), two pedestrians on the upper-left (1.8 m) and mid-right (0.8–1.2 m, near the wearer's right arm's reach) in frame 2, two pedestrians ahead on the upper-left (1.4 m) and upper-right (2.2 m, about 1.8 m apart) in frame 3, two similarly positioned figures in frame 4 (1.3 m left and 2.0 m right), and one pedestrian on the upper-right (1.8 m) in frame 5 as the wearer steps forward. Every surrounding person is heavily occluded by the top and side boundaries of the field of view—cutting off their upper torsos and heads so it is impossible to see if anyone looks toward the camera wearer—while the wearer's own green shirt partially occludes their striding legs below. While the map makes it easier than the RGB image to count and bound the partially visible people at the edges of the frame, it provides no ground layout or distance cues of its own. It is also unreliable in several places: in frame 1 it completely misses the pedestrian walking ahead at the top center, and in frame 4 it over-segments the camera wearer's left arm into two overlapping `person` instances while misclassifying the pedestrian's legs on the upper right as a `dog`.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only pairs of magenta 2D hand skeletons for the camera wearer's own left and right hands in frames 3 and 5. In those two frames, the wearer's hands are positioned below the camera in the lower half of the view at roughly 0.5–0.7 m distance (within the wearer's immediate arm's reach) and spaced about 0.4–0.5 m apart horizontally as the arms swing during walking. Because the map fails to render any yellow body skeletons, it provides no spatial information about the scene layout, the wearer's torso and legs, or the multiple surrounding pedestrians located 0.8–2.5 m away who are partially cut off at the top and side edges of the RGB frames. Consequently, relative positions, facing directions, gaze, and approach or retreat trajectories across time cannot be determined from this map alone. What little it does show is the precise articulation of the wearer's curled fingers in frames 3 and 5, which stand out more clearly against the black background than against the textured bricks in RGB, but the map is highly unreliable under this steep downward egocentric angle, missing the wearer's hands in frames 1, 2, and 4 as well as the nearby pedestrian's right hand in frame 2.
